grade.primary_choice: Keep Ruby/Rails/Sidekiq; profile, then add parallelism with one process per core, make each image cheaper, and autoscale on queue depth
unsupported_claims: The 5–10% CPU saving from a Go or Rust rewrite is an unmeasured guess, though the answer calls it a guess.
'Each Sidekiq thread holds a database connection' is loosely worded: threads take a connection from a shared pool only when they use the database.
grade.notes: The answer works out from CPU-hours versus wall-clock time that the run was nearly serial, rejects a rewrite because of where the CPU time goes and because the founder reviews the code, and covers profiling, GVL and VIPS_CONCURRENCY, autoscaling on queue depth and separate bulk queues. Its tagging-model advice is weaker: it covers small input size and batching but leaves out quantisation, ONNX Runtime and loading the model once per process, and it skips spot instances and the managed tagging API option.
